headline: Gains fade as core exploration losses continue
summary_short: Ivanhoe Electric reported a Q2 FY2026 net loss of $24.65 million (-$0.16/share diluted), reversing Q1's $124.7 million one-off gain from the Alacrán project sale, while cash held at $256.9 million.
summary_long: Q2 FY2026's $24.65 million net loss (-$0.16/share) followed Q1's outsized $124.7 million gain on Cordoba's sale of its remaining Alacrán Copper Project stake — a one-off, not an operating trend reversal. Exploration spending rose $7.3 million y/y to $21.4 million, concentrated at Santa Cruz, Gleeson and Hog Heaven drilling programs. An $8.0 million gain on the April divestment of the Pinaya Gold-Copper Project partly offset the increase, but not enough to avoid a loss. Cash fell to $256.9 million from $289.8 million q/q on Santa Cruz build-out spending, though it remains far above year-ago levels on the Alacrán proceeds. No revenue guidance was issued; CGI licensing revenue, the company's only revenue source, slipped to $0.7 million.
confidence_notes: Prior-quarter (Q1 FY2026) operating income (+$96.8M) and net income (+$41.7M) reflect a one-off $124.7 million gain on Cordoba's sale of its remaining 50% interest in the Alacrán Copper Project (closed March 5, 2026, $128M gross proceeds) plus a $5.0 million credit-loss provision reversal — not a recurring operating trend. The filing's own MD&A confirms this: 'the most significant contributor to this change...was the gain of $124.7 million being realized on Cordoba's sale of the Alacrán Copper Project.' This quarter (Q2) carries a smaller, separate $8.0 million gain on the April 27, 2026 divestment of the Pinaya Gold-Copper Project, already netted into the reported operating/net loss. EPS in the shard follows the filing's own 'Net loss (income) per share' presentation (positive = loss, negative = income, consistent with Q1's gain quarter); flipped here to standard sign convention (negative = loss) for consistency with the net income figures. Ivanhoe Electric is a pre-revenue-stage minerals exploration and development company (Santa Cruz Copper Project, Arizona, is the primary asset); the ~$0.7M of revenue is licensing/data-processing fees from its CGI subsidiary and is non-core to the investment thesis.

drivers.explanation: Q1's outsized $124.7M Alacrán divestment gain didn't repeat; this quarter's smaller $8.0M Pinaya gain wasn't enough to offset a $7.3M y/y rise in exploration spending and $2.2M more equity-method JV losses.
Same driver: absence of the one-off $124.7M Alacrán gain booked in Q1, only partly offset by the $8.0M Pinaya divestment gain and no repeat of Q2 2025's $2.6M impairment.
Tracks net income; Q1's gain-driven per-share income reversed to a $0.16 per-share loss this quarter.

q/q decline reflects continued cash outflows for Santa Cruz Copper Project infrastructure/equipment deposits ($20.9M) and the Maaden Joint Venture ($6.3M) during H1, not fully offset by ongoing project financing.

CGI's software licensing and data-processing revenue (100% of total) fell to $0.7M from $1.1M a year earlier due to less data processing services being performed; not explained further in the release.

Management frames the quarter around project advancement, not earnings: exploration spend concentrated on Santa Cruz Copper Project permitting and an updated PFS (expected Q3 2026), plus drilling at Gleeson and Hog Heaven.
